Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with a knee injury consistent in type and mechanism with the force of
the impact. Over the course of 29 visits, care followed a standard progression of conservative management, including physical
therapy, activity modification, and anti-inflammatory medication. Frequency of visits tapered as symptoms improved and
functional capacity returned. Examination findings are mixed: several orthopedic tests reproduced pain and support the reported
injury, while other assessments, including neurovascular checks and ligamentous stability testing, returned normal results.
Review of the medical history shows treatment to the same knee area within the past two years; that prior condition contributes to
some of the current complaints and has been considered in the overall assessment. Billing records show two similar charges
posted on the same date, which are currently under review for accuracy. Ongoing monitoring is recommended, with reassessment
at the next scheduled visit.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
